# The Bus

The mesh has one structural component: a **publish/subscribe proxy** that connects publishers to subscribers by topic. No actor knows about any other actor. There are no direct connections.

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as actor A
  participant B as actor B
  participant C as client
  participant BUS as pub/sub proxy
  participant X as actor X
  participant Y as actor Y
  participant Z as actor Z

  A ->> BUS : topic=orders
  BUS ->> X : topic=orders
  BUS ->> Z : topic=orders

  B ->> BUS : topic=alerts
  BUS ->> Y : topic=alerts
  BUS ->> Z : topic=alerts

  C ->> BUS : topic=orders
  BUS ->> X : topic=orders
  BUS ->> Z : topic=orders
```

A message published on topic `orders` reaches every subscriber of `orders` — including actors that don't exist yet when the sender runs.

::: {.callout}
**The proxy is not a broker.** It holds no queues, makes no routing decisions, and persists nothing. It is a wire junction. Durability, ordering, and acknowledgement are concerns of the actors themselves.
:::

## How it works

The proxy is a single NNG device — a sub0 socket forward to a pub0 socket via `nng_device()`. Publishers dial the sub port, subscribers dial the pub port. NNG's pub0/sub0 does prefix matching on the message body, which begins with the `topic[32]` field of the tuple header. Subscriber-side filtering means every actor sees every message on the wire and drops what it isn't subscribed to — a single `memcmp` per message.

::: {.callout}
**Topic-level isolation** is achieved by encrypting sensitive payloads. The topic field is public — anyone on the bus can see that a message on topic `sql_query` was sent. But the payload bytes are opaque and can be encrypted end-to-end between the publishing actor and the intended handler.
:::

## The proxy is an actor

The proxy is a special-case actor. It has no handler, no LMDB, and no topic subscription — but it participates in the mesh like any other member: it emits on the `heartbeat` topic at `PROXY_HEARTBEAT_MS` intervals and responds to `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` for clean shutdown. This makes the proxy itself observable and liveness-checkable via the same heartbeat mechanism as all other actors.

## Endpoints

The proxy binds two NNG sockets and forwards all messages between them in a tight recv → send loop:

- **sub** on `tcp://*:5557` — actors and clients publish here
- **pub** on `tcp://*:5556` — actors and clients subscribe here

Both endpoints accept multiple transports simultaneously. Bind WebSocket alongside TCP to support browser clients with no extra bridging:

```sh
PROXY_SUB_BIND=tcp://*:5557,ws://*:8080
PROXY_PUB_BIND=tcp://*:5556,ws://*:8081
```

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROXY_SUB_BIND` | `tcp://*:5557` | Actors publish here (proxy receives) |
| `PROXY_PUB_BIND` | `tcp://*:5556` | Actors subscribe here (proxy fans out) |
| `PROXY_ID` | `proxy` | Identity used in heartbeat emission |
| `PROXY_HEARTBEAT_MS` | `5000` | Heartbeat interval ms. `0` to disable |
